sources.title: Situation Report on the Crisis in Haiti, July–August 2026
sources.temporal_coverage: Retain the dated scope of individual claims; no extrapolation to present conditions.
sources.methodology: Substantive publisher operational summary for July–August 2026.
sources.limitations: Not a climate-attribution study or representative protection survey.

claims.paraphrase: UNICEF reports May 2025 heavy rains inundated about 3,900 homes in Nord-Est; Melissa later damaged schools, latrines and water systems especially in southern departments.
claims.limitations: Dated operational estimates, not climate-change attribution.

claims.paraphrase: Following Melissa, UNICEF reports cholera outbreaks in Bainet, Marigot, Belle-Anse, Grand-Gosier and Thiotte, exposing vulnerabilities where climate shocks damaged services.
claims.limitations: Temporal association and reported cases, not attributable disease burden.

claims.locator: Physical PDF p.2, armed violence and displacement paragraphs.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF reports violence-driven site growth after Mirebalais/Saut d’Eau attacks and displacement in Petite-Rivière; most displaced people lived outside formal sites or with hosts.

claims.locator: Physical PDF p.2, humanitarian access paragraph.
claims.paraphrase: UNFPA reports November 2025 insecurity postponed planned distributions and mobile clinics, including support for hurricane-affected women/girls around Petit-Goâve and southern areas.
claims.limitations: Reported implementation constraint, not a current route assessment.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Violence restricted delivery of health/protection support during hurricane response.

claims.locator: Physical PDF p.2, hurricane impact paragraph.
claims.paraphrase: Melissa damaged Grand’Anse roads and isolated communal sections; Les Cayes hospital flooding and minor Jérémie/Port-de-Paix damage were reported separately from insecurity restrictions.
claims.limitations: Weather and violence access constraints must not be conflated.

claims.paraphrase: UNFPA reports mobile clinics reached 2,453 Melissa-affected people in Petit-Goâve, alongside separate internally displaced populations in metropolitan and Artibonite sites.
claims.limitations: Operational reach, not unique national coverage or evaluated impact.

claims.locator: Physical PDF pp.2–3, response and kits/hotline sections.
claims.paraphrase: UNFPA maintained GBV hotlines/referrals and mobile services despite access barriers; reproductive-health kits supplied facilities, while projected coverage was an intended benefit.
claims.limitations: Activities and intended coverage are not protection-effect estimates.

claims.locator: Observed-context section, paragraphs on insecurity and Melissa.
claims.paraphrase: The October 2025 assessment reports gang passage fees and restricted agricultural-input delivery along RN1/RN2/RN3, while Melissa separately flooded displacement sites in metropolitan Port-au-Prince.
claims.limitations: Compounding pressures, not an identified interaction effect.

claims.locator: Observed-context section, Sud-Est road damage paragraph.
claims.paraphrase: Melissa road damage disrupted Jacmel–Port-au-Prince connections and Belle-Anse/Marigot supply and emergency-access routes.
claims.limitations: Historical access disruption, not present route guidance.

claims.paraphrase: FEWS NET reports funding-related inability to preposition cyclone-season food, compounded by violence-related access interruptions and logistics costs near displacement sites.
claims.limitations: Multi-driver monitoring account, not a causal programme evaluation.

claims.paraphrase: UNFPA’s August 2026 snapshot reports violence displacement in Kenscoff, Dessalines and Petite-Rivière and constrained access to prompt care for sexual-violence survivors.
claims.limitations: Violence context, not climate-caused displacement or current incidence.

claims.locator: Publisher summary, service and funding paragraphs.
claims.paraphrase: In July–August 2026, UNFPA reports delivering SRH and GBV services where access was possible, but financing remained well below its appeal.
claims.limitations: Reported outputs and funding, not outcome evidence.

gaps: Melissa impact counts vary across agencies and reporting dates; source-specific snapshots are not pooled or treated as present caseloads.
UNFPA and UNICEF service outputs do not establish independent protection effectiveness, avoided losses or climate-change attribution.
